product_category: AI 3D model generation platform (text, image and sketch to textured, rigged, print-ready 3D models, with plugins, API and a studio workspace)
description: A fictional market of 100 buyers for an AI 3D generation platform, split evenly across four segments: amateurs, individual pros and startups, SMB game studios and large studios. Each company carries the buying committee its segment really has: one person for an amateur, one or two for a pro or startup, five for an SMB studio and seven for a large studio. Every persona's pain points are drawn from the Meshy persona doc, the messaging teardown and a review readout of 1,828 Trustpilot and G2 reviews, with intensity that varies by company. All names and companies are invented.

themes.ip: Ownership, licensed training data, indemnity, provenance

themes.credits: Credit burn, billing surprises, refunds, checkout
themes.craft: Authorship, style, pride in the work
themes.jobs: Fear of AI replacing artists, team morale
themes.compliance: Security reviews, audits, contracts, AI policies
themes.support: Getting help, response time, a named contact
themes.differentiation: Standing out, looking bigger, winning clients
themes.revenue: Selling more, shipping more, growing the business

roles.label: Weekend maker
roles.context: Owns a 3D printer and makes miniatures, figures and gifts. Can't model or use CAD. Pays with a personal card and reads the checkout page closely.

core_pains.label: Can't model or use CAD
core_pains.description: Has ideas and sketches but no way to turn them into a printable file without learning CAD.

core_pains.label: Fear of a surprise charge
core_pains.description: Has heard about AI tools that bill annually when the plan looked monthly, and refunds that bounce.

optional_pains.label: Prints that fail
optional_pains.description: Models that aren't watertight waste filament and an evening.

optional_pains.label: Locked downloads
optional_pains.description: Generating a model, then hitting a paywall to download it.

optional_pains.label: Wants it to feel like theirs
optional_pains.description: Wants the villain at the table to be their idea, not something an AI made.

optional_pains.label: Credits burned on bad results
optional_pains.description: Failed or off-prompt generations still cost credits.

roles.label: Hobby game builder
roles.context: Builds games on weekends in Unity, Godot or Roblox Studio. Needs props and a character or two, not a 3D course.

core_pains.label: Needs assets, not a 3D course
core_pains.description: Scenes sit empty because modeling takes too long to learn.

core_pains.label: Free tier won't export
core_pains.description: Worries the free plan won't let them export or use what they made.

optional_pains.label: Feels like an impostor
optional_pains.description: Next to real developers, worries the game looks amateur.

optional_pains.label: Imports break in the engine
optional_pains.description: Models that look fine in a preview come in broken or too heavy.

optional_pains.label: Tiny budget
optional_pains.description: Twenty dollars a month is a real decision.

roles.label: Student creator
roles.context: An adult college student building class projects and a first portfolio. Often on a tight budget, sometimes with a school discount.

core_pains.label: Price
core_pains.description: Every subscription competes with rent and textbooks.

core_pains.label: Wants a portfolio that stands out
core_pains.description: Needs work that looks like their own style, not generic AI output.

optional_pains.label: Credits run out mid-project
optional_pains.description: Monthly credits expire or run out the week a project is due.

optional_pains.label: Unclear if AI is allowed
optional_pains.description: Not sure if instructors accept AI-assisted work.

optional_pains.label: Steep learning curve
optional_pains.description: Blender tutorials take more hours than the project allows.

roles.label: Solo commercial dev
roles.context: Ships games on Steam, mobile or Roblox with one to five people. Buys on a card, compares the cost per asset to a contractor quote, and posts devlogs.

core_pains.label: No budget for a 3D artist
core_pains.description: Needs a whole cast of characters and props that one person can't model in time.

core_pains.label: Assets that look AI-made
core_pains.description: Fears playtesters and Steam reviewers will clock the art as AI and discount the game.

optional_pains.label: Consistency across a set
optional_pains.description: Props from different runs don't look like they belong in the same world.

optional_pains.label: Rigging on odd proportions
optional_pains.description: Stylized and chibi characters deform badly when rigged.

optional_pains.label: Credits run out in crunch
optional_pains.description: Monthly credits vanish the week before a demo.

optional_pains.label: Commercial rights
optional_pains.description: Needs clean title to every asset before a store or publisher asks.

roles.label: Freelance 3D artist
roles.context: Already models for a living in Blender or ZBrush. Clients want more options in less time. Pride in craft makes them wary of AI tools.

core_pains.label: Clients want more options faster
core_pains.description: Every brief asks for three variations by Friday at the same rate.

core_pains.label: Fear of being devalued
core_pains.description: Worries AI makes clients think the work should cost less.

optional_pains.label: Cleanup eats the time saved
optional_pains.description: Dense, uneven topology means retopology before anything is usable.

optional_pains.label: Signature style
optional_pains.description: Clients hire them for a look; generic output dilutes it.

optional_pains.label: Client rights questions
optional_pains.description: Clients ask who owns AI-assisted work and whether it trained a model.

roles.label: Agent builder
roles.context: Wires 3D into AI workflows through APIs and MCP, using Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. Judges docs, rate limits and predictability before anything else.

core_pains.label: Agent can't make real meshes
core_pains.description: Code-built primitives aren't good enough for the product.

core_pains.label: Unpredictable API cost
core_pains.description: Bulk generation burns credits with no cost shown before the call.

optional_pains.label: API assets missing from the workspace
optional_pains.description: Assets made through the API don't show up in the web workspace, so the team tracks them by hand.

optional_pains.label: Could build it myself
optional_pains.description: Tempted to wire an open model instead of paying for a platform.

optional_pains.label: Rate limits
optional_pains.description: Needs to know the platform holds up at volume.

roles.label: Product-visual founder
roles.context: Runs an e-commerce, AR or app team that needs 3D product and brand assets at volume. Wants the product to look premium and the company to look bigger than it is.

core_pains.label: Polycount too high for the web
core_pains.description: Models load slowly on product pages and in AR.

core_pains.label: Cost at volume
core_pains.description: Hundreds of SKUs at agency rates is out of the question.

optional_pains.label: Wants to look bigger
optional_pains.description: Needs visuals that compete with brands ten times their size.

optional_pains.label: Product accuracy
optional_pains.description: A 3D model that gets the product wrong creates returns.

optional_pains.label: Rights to brand assets
optional_pains.description: Needs to know the brand's assets stay private and owned.

roles.label: Print shop owner
roles.context: Sells 3D-printed products on Etsy, Shopify or to local clients. Margins depend on how fast a design goes from idea to a print that works.

core_pains.label: New designs are the bottleneck
core_pains.description: Printers sit idle while the next product waits for a model.

core_pains.label: Failed prints cost margin
core_pains.description: A model that isn't watertight wastes filament and a print slot.

optional_pains.label: Custom orders take too long
optional_pains.description: Customers want their pet, logo or character printed, and quoting takes days.

optional_pains.label: Owning the designs they sell
optional_pains.description: Can't sell a product they don't have clear rights to.

optional_pains.label: Standing out on Etsy
optional_pains.description: Hundreds of shops sell the same models from free libraries.

roles.label: Studio head
roles.context: Owns budget, runway and the publisher relationship. Cares how the studio treats its people and doesn't want to be the studio that replaced its artists.

core_pains.label: Cost per asset
core_pains.description: Art is the biggest line in the budget, and outsourcing quotes keep rising.

core_pains.label: What to tell the publisher
core_pains.description: Needs a defensible answer when the publisher asks how the studio uses generative AI.

optional_pains.label: Keeping the artists' respect
optional_pains.description: Fears the team will read any AI tool as a step toward layoffs.

optional_pains.label: Runway
optional_pains.description: Every month of slip costs real money.

optional_pains.label: Player backlash
optional_pains.description: A public 'they used AI art' story could hurt the launch.

roles.label: Art director
roles.context: Owns the asset pipeline and the art bar. Under pressure on props per artist-week, and doesn't want a tool that creates cleanup work or angers the team.

core_pains.label: Prop backlog
core_pains.description: Hundreds of background props are due before the milestone.

core_pains.label: Tools that create cleanup
core_pains.description: Dense topology and inconsistent results mean artists spend the saved time fixing output.

optional_pains.label: Holding the art bar
optional_pains.description: Pride in the studio's look turns into fear of a quality drop.

optional_pains.label: Seniors stuck on grind work
optional_pains.description: Senior artists spend weeks on crates instead of hero characters.

optional_pains.label: Textures break under engine lighting
optional_pains.description: Baked shadows and seams show up in Unreal and Unity.

optional_pains.label: Team pushback
optional_pains.description: Half the team is against AI and will judge the pilot harshly.

roles.label: Environment artist
roles.context: Their eye and craft are their identity, and their community calls AI theft. They decide whether a pilot survives week one.

core_pains.label: AI coming for the job
core_pains.description: Watched layoffs across the industry and reads every AI tool as a threat.

core_pains.label: Authorship
core_pains.description: If a machine made it, is it still their work?

optional_pains.label: Their work training a model
optional_pains.description: Won't touch a tool that learns from what they make.

optional_pains.label: Burnout on grind work
optional_pains.description: Weeks of crates and barrels before anything creative.

optional_pains.label: 500k-triangle meshes
optional_pains.description: Has seen AI meshes that take longer to fix than to model.

roles.label: Tech artist
roles.context: Owns DCC plugins, export, poly budgets and rigging. Distrusts black boxes and wants limits set before generation, not fixed after.

core_pains.label: Poly budgets and topology
core_pains.description: Needs quad topology and a target poly count, not cleanup after the fact.

core_pains.label: Black-box results
core_pains.description: The same prompt gives a clean mesh one run and a broken one the next.

optional_pains.label: Engine-safe PBR
optional_pains.description: Baked lighting in textures breaks under the engine's lights.

optional_pains.label: Plugin and export fit
optional_pains.description: Every new tool has to work with the existing Unity or Unreal pipeline.

optional_pains.label: Predictable cost per asset
optional_pains.description: Wants the cost of each generation shown before the click.

roles.label: Producer
roles.context: Owns milestones and vendor spend. Will back anything that saves the schedule, and kill anything that drags a pilot past a milestone.

core_pains.label: Milestones slipping
core_pains.description: Background assets are the first thing to slip the schedule.

core_pains.label: Vendor spend
core_pains.description: Outsourcing invoices keep coming in over budget.

optional_pains.label: Pilots that drag
optional_pains.description: Tool pilots with no fixed scope eat weeks.

optional_pains.label: A vendor who shows up
optional_pains.description: Needs a named contact and a same-day answer during crunch.

roles.label: VP of Art
roles.context: Owns the art budget, headcount plan and a franchise's visual legacy. Believes the quality bar is higher than a playtest.

core_pains.label: Content volume up, headcount flat
core_pains.description: Live-service updates need more assets every quarter with the same team.

core_pains.label: A quality bar AI can't meet
core_pains.description: Doubts generated assets survive art review on a flagship title.

optional_pains.label: Outsourcing cost and lead time
optional_pains.description: External art takes months and costs more each year.

optional_pains.label: Artists' work absorbed by a model
optional_pains.description: Won't approve anything that trains on the studio's art.

optional_pains.label: Rivals shipping faster
optional_pains.description: Watched a competitor double its content cadence.

roles.label: CTO or technical director
roles.context: Owns pipeline, tools and vendor architecture. Weighs building or self-hosting against renting a platform.

core_pains.label: Build or self-host instead
core_pains.description: An open model like Hunyuan3D runs on their own servers for free.

core_pains.label: API scale and uptime
core_pains.description: Needs throughput, consistency and SSO at studio scale.

optional_pains.label: Vendor lock-in
optional_pains.description: Doesn't want the pipeline to depend on one startup.

optional_pains.label: Inconsistent output at scale
optional_pains.description: Results vary too much to automate.

optional_pains.label: Retention controls
optional_pains.description: Needs control over where data lives and how long.

roles.label: R&D lead
roles.context: Runs tool evaluations and has often tried Meshy on a side project. Needs a documented pilot win to take upward.

core_pains.label: Repeatable results
core_pains.description: Can't champion a tool that gives different results on the same input.

core_pains.label: A pilot win to show upward
core_pains.description: Needs numbers leadership will believe.

optional_pains.label: A named vendor contact
optional_pains.description: Pilots stall when nobody answers technical questions.

optional_pains.label: Rivals already using AI
optional_pains.description: Hears competitors use AI tools and doesn't want to fall behind.

optional_pains.label: Internal politics
optional_pains.description: Every AI pilot becomes a debate about jobs.

roles.label: Legal and IP counsel
roles.context: Owns contracts, indemnity and the AI policy. Proud of never being wrong, and will hold a deal for months over unclear provenance.

core_pains.label: Training-data provenance
core_pains.description: Needs proof the model was trained on licensed data, in writing.

core_pains.label: Indemnity
core_pains.description: Wants the vendor to stand behind the output if a claim lands.

optional_pains.label: Publisher contract breach
optional_pains.description: A generative AI clause in the publisher contract creates exposure.

optional_pains.label: Studio inputs used for training
optional_pains.description: Concept art and references must never train a vendor's model.

optional_pains.label: The AI addendum
optional_pains.description: A 40-question addendum that most vendors can't answer cleanly.

roles.label: InfoSec
roles.context: Owns vendor risk. Unreleased game assets leaving the building is a nightmare scenario.

core_pains.label: Unreleased assets leaving the building
core_pains.description: A leak of unannounced content would be front-page news.

core_pains.label: Audit reports
core_pains.description: Needs SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reports before anything else.

optional_pains.label: SSO and access control
optional_pains.description: Every tool must sit behind the studio's identity provider.

optional_pains.label: Data location and retention
optional_pains.description: Needs to know where data lives and set how long it's kept.

roles.label: Procurement
roles.context: Owns MSAs, pricing and onboarding. Defaults to no when the paper doesn't fit the template.

core_pains.label: Non-standard terms
core_pains.description: Startup paper that doesn't fit the MSA template stalls for months.

core_pains.label: Volume pricing and invoicing
core_pains.description: Credit-card plans and credit packs don't fit how the studio buys.

optional_pains.label: Vendor sprawl
optional_pains.description: Every team wants its own AI tool.

optional_pains.label: Startup vendor risk
optional_pains.description: Worried the vendor won't be around in three years.

roles.label: Senior artist
roles.context: Speaks for the team's morale and often for guild sentiment. 28% of GDC 2026 respondents were laid off in two years, and it shows.

core_pains.label: Layoffs
core_pains.description: Every efficiency tool feels like a headcount plan.

core_pains.label: Credit for the work
core_pains.description: Wants artists to keep control and credit, with AI on grind work only.

optional_pains.label: AI as theft
optional_pains.description: Believes most models were trained on artists' work without consent.

optional_pains.label: Guild and community pressure
optional_pains.description: Peers will judge anyone who endorses an AI tool.

art_director.label: Live-service content cadence
art_director.description: A content update every six weeks never lets the backlog clear.

producer.label: Update cadence
producer.description: Every update date is fixed and public.

vp_art.label: Margin per asset
vp_art.description: Competes on price and turnaround; AI decides who wins the next bid.

legal.label: Proving clean AI use to clients
legal.description: Studio clients demand proof that delivered assets are clean.

legal.label: Exposure across the portfolio
legal.description: One studio's AI misstep becomes the publisher's problem.

print_shop.label: Marketplace AI rules
print_shop.description: Etsy and other marketplaces ask sellers to disclose AI-assisted designs.

studio_head.label: Every hire matters
studio_head.description: With 30 people, one artist leaving stalls a whole area of the game.
